2609.08779.title: Improving Term Evaluation in Machine Translation: Variation Matters
2609.08779.paper_summary: Terminology evaluation in machine translation (MT) usually assumes a single correct target form per source term. However, human translators routinely introduce variation that current metrics penalize as inconsistency. We examine how to account for this variation in document-level MT evaluation of English-French scientific translation, combining glossary-based accuracy, translation consistency, and a new cross-term variation (CTV) diagnostic measure that tests whether variation relationships are preserved across languages. Based on analyses of two parallel corpora, translated by four MT systems, we find that (1) MT systems generate less target-side variation than human translators; (2) transfer patterns strongly depend on the variation type; (3) consistency rankings vary with the choice of metric; and (4) constraining MT with a glossary improves accuracy and consistency but degrades CTV by suppressing valid variation. We argue for variation-aware evaluation that conditions consistency penalties on whether target-side variation mirrors source-side variation.
2609.08779.paper_summary_zh: 術語評估在機器翻譯（MT）中通常假設每個源術語只有一個正確的目標形式。<lb/>然而，人類翻譯者常常引入變化，而當前的度量標準將其懲罰為不一致性。<lb/>我們研究如何在英法科學翻譯的文檔級MT評估中考慮這種變化，結合基於詞彙表的準確性、翻譯一致性以及一種新的跨術語變化（CTV）診斷測量，該測量測試變化關係是否在不同語言之間得以保留。<lb/>根據對由四個MT系統翻譯的兩個平行語料庫的分析，我們發現（1）MT系統產生的目標側變化少於人類翻譯者；（2）轉移模式強烈依賴於變化類型；（3）一致性排名隨著度量標準的選擇而變化；（4）使用詞彙表約束MT提高了準確性和一致性，但通過抑制有效變化而降低了CTV。<lb/>我們主張應進行變化意識的評估，將一致性懲罰的條件建立在目標側變化是否反映源側變化的基礎上。
